name: laravel
description: Finds the mistakes a Laravel application gives away in its own traffic: debug mode left on (the Ignition or Whoops page and the JSON exception reply, with the stack traces, server environment and APP_KEY they print), the development tooling left reachable (Telescope, Horizon, Pulse, Debugbar, Clockwork, Ignition's routes, log viewers), the files a document root pointed at the project rather than public/ exposes (.env, composer.json, storage logs, vendor), and session cookies missing Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite. It reads traffic that has already passed and records what it finds as findings. An opt-in check, off by default, requests a short list of Laravel paths once per origin on in-scope hosts.

settings.label: Check the session cookies' attributes
settings.description: Report a Laravel session, remember-me or CSRF cookie that is missing Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite, or that is sent unencrypted. Each is one finding per cookie per host.

settings.label: Record an APP_KEY the app prints
settings.description: An APP_KEY found in an error page or an exposed .env is recorded as a hidden finding, so it is masked on screen until you click the eye beside it. Off: the leak is still reported, but the key itself is not stored.

settings.label: Request a short list of Laravel paths
settings.description: Off: the plugin is entirely passive and reports only what the traffic already carried. On: when a host is shown to run Laravel, it requests the paths below once — this is active testing, it reaches the target, and it is kept to the hosts your targets cover. A host is asked once per engagement and never again: what was asked is written into the engagement, so reloading the plugin, restarting reProxy or browsing the site a second time sends nothing more. The requests are recorded in the Traffic list, and the result is noted on the origin in the Entity Explorer (laravel-checked).

settings.label: Paths the active check requests
settings.description: Requested once per host, relative to its root, when the active check is on. Changing the list does not re-check a host that has already been checked in this engagement.

settings.label: Largest body read (KiB)
settings.description: A response bigger than this is left unread. Error pages with a full stack trace are large, but the whole body has to be searched, so the cap is what keeps the work inside a plugin's time budget.
